coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Potrero Power Station Block 12
record.summary: Planned commercial block on the Potrero Power Station masterplan (the design guidelines permit office and laboratory/life-science uses), paired with Block 11 in the project engineer's description of about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking; design under review as of the March 2025 annual compliance report, with no construction start found.

notes.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- this block is not yet built and does not correspond to any subdivided Assessor parcel: it currently sits on vacant/graded land within the former power station site (unaddressed in DataSF's Assessor roll). Traced from an adopted regulatory diagram by fitting it to multiple real street points (see the mapping log), but this diagram is dated 2020 and may not reflect later design changes. Treat vertex positions as accurate to roughly 10-25m, not survey-grade. South edge corrected 2026-09-16 using the source diagram's own measured depth -- should be reliable to within a few meters, but has NOT been independently confirmed against a visible real-world curb. Rebuilt 2026-09-16 by re-fitting the diagram to real street points. Re-measured 2026-09-16 (a third time) in a single consistent measurement across the whole block layout. Re-corrected 2026-09-16 (a fourth time) after fixing a mis-measured reference point. That the block is not yet built is consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025), which says vertical applications are under review for Blocks 11 and 12; the vacant/graded and unaddressed-in-Assessor-roll wording is Pier & Point's own observation. The 2020 date of the diagram is confirmed by the final D4D's footer (February 26, 2020). How this shape was traced, including earlier versions, is logged in its data file in the public data repository (https://github.com/pierandpoint/record).
notes.digitized_from: Potrero Power Station Design for Development, Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (p.245).
notes.why_no_real_parcel: A real Assessor parcel may exist under this block (part of the site's larger, largely unaddressed footprint), but it has not been subdivided per the masterplan's individual named blocks -- this uses hand-traced approximate geometry instead. (This reflects Pier & Point's own parcel search, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)
notes.regulatory_context: Flat 100 ft max height per Figure 6.2.3. Paired with Block 11 on the project's MEP engineer's page (Meyers+), which describes the two blocks together as about 430,000 sq ft of office with below-grade parking (see that entry for the combined GSF estimate); the final D4D's Table 3.1.1 permits laboratory and life-science uses on Block 12, but no cited source calls the pair a life-science campus. No construction-start source found; the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) says vertical applications for Blocks 11 and 12 were under review.

facts.value: Non-Retail Sales/Services (office) and Laboratory/Life Science uses permitted; Residential Not Permitted under the adopted D4D final Table 3.1.1 (a 2026 proposed DA amendment would add residential flexibility here -- see milestones)
flat 100 ft max per the D4D's Figure 6.2.3
Blocks 11 and 12 combined: approximately 430,000 sq ft of office, with below-grade parking, per the project's MEP engineer
Herzog & de Meuron + Adamson (Blocks 11, 12 and 15 together)
Seeking LEED Gold certification; designed as an all-electric building

Bus shelter and transit operator restroom delivered with Block 12, per the Phasing Table; a 100% Schematic Design plan set incorporating SFMTA/Public Works feedback was sent to those agencies January 7, 2022
Listed as part of Phase 1 in the 2024 annual compliance report ('Phase 1 includes Blocks 2, 7, 8, 11, 12, and 15...')

milestones.text: Board of Supervisors approves the Potrero Power Station project and Development Agreement (Ordinance No. 62-20, Board File 200040), the entitlement covering the adopted Design for Development, whose Land Use Table (Table 3.1.1) lists Block 12 (the Planning Commission had voted 5-0 on January 30, 2020 to recommend approval of the project); the Development Agreement's own effective date is May 25, 2020, distinct from the D4D's own February 26, 2020 final-document date. (Block 12 was later named one of Phase 1's six blocks by the October 2020 Phase 1 Development Phase Application -- a construction-phase assignment, not when it first entered the plan.)

open_questions: No design review approval or construction-start date found for Block 12; the most recent primary source found (the 2024 annual compliance report) describes design as 'under review', not approved.

The combined 430,000 sq ft figure for Blocks 11+12 comes from the project's MEP engineer, not a Planning Department document; no Planning Commission or Planning Director approval memo for Block 12 was found to confirm or break out this figure.

The Chronicle's July 2026 report of a proposed +23 ft height increase and added residential flexibility is tied to a pending Development Agreement/Planning Code amendment (BOS Files 260724 and 260770) that had not been adopted as of this dossier's last-verified date.

Whether Blocks 11 and 12 are described as a life-science campus anywhere: the only source that pairs them (Meyers+) describes about 430,000 sq ft of office; the D4D permits laboratory/life-science use on Block 12 but no cited source says that is the plan.

Corrected 2026-10-06 (accuracy audit, October 2026): the July 2026 Development Agreement amendment request was shown as an expected event after it had been made and heard; it is now shown as having happened, with the Planning Commission's unanimous approval (SF Standard, August 3, 2026). Board of Supervisors action is still to be confirmed.
